articleTitle: The Influence Of Refractive MDEX Variation of Troposphere in Midolle and Hidh Latitudes on Radiosignal Fluctuations
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problems concerned space and time variation of radiometeorological parameters of terrestnial atmosphere and their imfluence on fluctuation chavacteristics of radiosignals in diffractional and tropospheric paths are considered in the paper. In different seasons of the year nigh and Ion field levels are shown to be in close correlation with seasonal variation of increased and decreased vertical gradients of the refractive index.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of cellular structures of the mobile communications systems
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Technical-economic indexes, characterizing the output quantity and quality and Joint economical expenses, combined in one index of efficiency with the measurement of <tex>$\frac{1 sq.km}{thous.roubl.}$</tex> show the expediency of establishing mobile communication networks based on the cellular structure. Multiple utilization of the identical frequencies in the system allows for expanding the service zone and enhance the system capacity without allotting additional frequency range. Specific expenses for one subscriber in the mobile cellular structure communication system with a heavy trafic are less than in analogous networks with a little operational trafic.

articleTitle: Dynamic Indices of Electromagnetic Compatibility at Nonsinusoidal Voltage
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the general case electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) should be estimated by influence of nonsinusoidal voltage upon the electric receivers. The universal SMC indices are established by the characteristics of process in the output of the dynamic system, which simulate basic properties of electric receivers. EMC estimation in the operating pomer networks should be performed by special instruments, with their block diagrams being the same as those in dynamic models.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Pulse Interference Attenuation with the Method of Extrapolation or Interpolation of Interfered Parts of Information
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Results of the study of effectiveness of some methods of short pulse interference attenuation are given. Comparison of these methods and recommendations on parameters of corresponding devices are described.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Fluctuations Model and Evaluation of Transmission Quality in Ground Wavs HF Propagation
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The fluctuation model of HF signals propagating above the ground in suburban area has been examined. The results ara presented proving the variability of signal envelope to be of ricean type. For this kind of model the error curves are constructed and the analysis of transmission accuracy is carried out.

articleTitle: Urban and Suburban Mobile Radio Propagation Characteristics in the VHF and UHF Bands
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Urban and suburban propagation problems at frequencies in the VHF and UHF bands are discussed. Propagation characteristics are presented; average attenuation factors are obtained and proposed for cellular mobile radio system statistical designing.

articleTitle: On the Choise of Spheric Radius of the Approximation of Obstacles
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The necessity of calculation of spheric radius approximation defending on wave lengths in case of flat in a radio path has been stated. Based on the results of experiments, carried out in the Gread Gobi Mongolia, it has been found, that for the determination of the spheric radius in the case it's enough to take it into consideration a third part of first Fresnel's zone in the UHF and VHF bands.

articleTitle: Future Applications of Vocoders and Spread Spectrum Equipment in Mobile Systems
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The structure of a digital radio-telephone system using vocoders and spread-spectrum equipment is aimed to enhance the effective utilization of spectrum allocated to mobile services. A comparative analysis of capacities for digital communication systems with frequency and code division is performed. Key problems associated with network synchronization are discussed.

articleTitle: Interference in Connectors of Transmission Lines of High-Speed Equipment
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with mechanism of interference in transmission lines of high-speed digital radioelectronic equipment due to nonhomogeneity of connectors. The analitical descriptions of arising interference and analog circuit of connectors substitutions causing these interferences are given. Means of interference reduction in connectors by introducing compensation and experimental data affirming its effectiveness are given.

articleTitle: Some Aspects of Frequency Management for HF and VHF Communication Equipment Groups
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Statistical method for the EMC evaluation of the group of closely arranged radio sets is proposed. The results of calculations for some typical configurations of HF and VHF radio sets are presented and compared with those analytically obtained by other authors. Data presented may be of use in designing communication systems and their optimization in respect of EMC.

articleTitle: Immunity and Efficiency of the Cellular Communication System Using Pulse-Code Modulation and Pseudo-Noise Signals
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Imunity characteristics of spread-spectrum cellular mobile radio system using PCM and pseudo-noise signals and functioning in a multipath channel with Rayleigh fading are presented. The advantages of such a system are demonstrated in comparison with a system using FM.

articleTitle: Arrangement for Improvement of the EMC of AM Broadcasting and Point-to-Point Communication Systems with the Help of Compensation of the Disturbance from the Interfering Radio Signals
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To struggle with the co-channel interfering signals, the compensation system may be used. Such systems allow for significant improvement of the EMC of communication device affected and for more efficient use of the radio spectrum. The paper presents the system consisting of two APC IP systems, the device to divide two voltages of variable sign, two phase shifters for 90° and a multiplier.

articleTitle: Investigation of Distribution of Currents Induced on Bioobjects Exposed in UHV Transmission Lines Electrical Fields
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Peculiarities of measuring currents induced on bioobjects exposed in UHV substations and transmission lines outdoor switch-gear electrical fields are considered. Technical data on instruments designed for solving this task and the results on induced current measurements obtained on volunteers are presented. Requirements for the circuits intended for measuring induced currents on alive objects are formulated.

articleTitle: Digital Method of Calculation of Stray Capacities of Radioelectronic Equipment Units of Complicated Configuration
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the method of calculation of stray capacities in structures of radioelectronic equipment based on design simulation by means of resistive grid with its calculation with the help of a computer. The main calculating relations for determining the parameters of the modal are given. Software algorithm on the step of electrical design parameters calculation mounted into the Computor Aided Design of radioelectronic equipments is described. This method is universal and can be applied for capacity calculations in systems of electrodes of rather complecated configuration in homogeneous or partially homogeneous medium. The above results of practical calculations affirm the high accuracy of this method.

articleTitle: Time Characteristics of Radio Interference
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The work is based on the results of experimental research of time statistical characteristics of EM interference on motor-highways and streets of towns. The dependence of these characteristics on the motor-transport movement intensity, methods of their forecasting and recommendations on use of this forecasting are given.

articleTitle: Description of Electromagnetic Interference on the Basis of a Theory of Systems with Random Structure
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic environment is essentially an inhomogenious process both in time and in space. It is suggested to consider each component of it as the result of some differential operator effect on the initial standard-process like "white noise" or Poisson sequence of delta pulses. A cumulative process of electromagnetic interference in the given point is described by its representation in the form of a response of a random structure dynamic system, in which at random moments of time the states of the system vary.

articleTitle: Radio Interference from Single CARS in VHF Wave Range
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Experimental results are given for the investigation of electromagnetic radiation created by single cars with ignition system. Spectral characteristics of the radiation in 1.5-3.0GHz frequency range have been measured at different observation angles of cars. Distribution functions of pulse interference amplitude values from vehicles have been obtained at fixed frequencies of the same wave range.

articleTitle: EM Coupling of Two Antennas
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: As a first step the two-dimensional problem is solved, concerning coupling of two antennas which are in the far zone from each other and between which is the half-plane with ideal conductivity. In the result of asymptotic calculation of the integral representation in the form of the plane wave spectrum, the uniform asymptotics of the coupling coefficient is found. As a generalization of this formula the uniform asymptotics for two antennas with an arbitrary form screen in the three-dimensional case is found. Asymptotic representation found for the coupling coefficient may be used for calculation of the coupling between paraboloid reflector antennas in the near zone /under the condition that exciters of antennas are in the far zone from each other/.

articleTitle: Forecasting of Information Reception Quality in Surface Mobile Radio Systems
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Te purpose of this work is to skow the use of interference environment forecast, published elsewhere by the author [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] together with the ultrashort wave signal characteristics forecast, for forecasting the quality of the information received by mobile stations of the surface, mobile radio systems, and al this on the stage of the design of these systems.

articleTitle: Cellular Public Radio Services Using Pseudo-Noise Signals
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Future development of cellular public radio systems and possibility of pseudo-noise signals application to them are discribed. Cochannel interference and spectrum efficiency are determined for phone message transmission.

articleTitle: Capacity of the Cellular Mobile Radio Service Using Pseudo-Noise Signals and Frequency Modulation
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Capacity of cellular mobile systema using pseudo-noise signals and FM is discussed. Total frequency band occupied by a system is determined as a function of system capasity for various cell radiuses.

articleTitle: Technical Parameters of Digital Transmission System
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deal with digital transmission system for SECAM colour television, with hit rate about 70 Mbit/s which enables the limitation of the frequency spectrum of transmitted digital signals without decreasing the quality of the analog picture reproduced. Tests carried out to determine basic parameters of this system were discussed, and results the values of the following parameters were determined: - kind of analog colour television signals to be sampled; - sampling frequency of luminance and colour-difference signals and number of samples per total line and per digital active line; - sampling structures; - technique of picture coding; - optimal algorithm of prediction composing; - number of quantization levels and the corresponding number of bits per sample. The remaining values of technical parameters were proposed, too.

articleTitle: Correlation Method of Determination of Interference Sources on the Object
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Determination of the interference source on an object during the the work of the radio system is important aspect of the EMC. The possibility of the use of correlation method for interference source identification is discussed. Method consists of measuring the correlation coefficient between interference source and videosignal after the detector of the receiver. It is not obcious if this method can be used when nonlinear effects are involved. The work discusses the correlation determination of interference source for the cases of blocking, intermodulation and crossmodulation in AM, PM and FM receiving sets. Correlation determination can be used in all cases, except that of phase manipulation.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Interference Influence on Satellite Communication Systems with the Multistation Access at Frequency Signal Division
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: On the basis of the formulae derived comparison is made of the satellite communication systems from the point of view of extent of the influence on them of broadband and narrowband interference.

articleTitle: Effect of Various Types of Interference on Useful Transmission. The Results of HF Receiver Simulation Testing
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The test was based on idealized model of HF receiver simulating the processing of input signals by its successive stages. The input signal was the sum of useful telegraphe signal and of interference in the form of noise, pulses or interfering signal. The following characteristics were calculated: - the output bit error rate and spectrum coverage factor as the function of input signals mutual offset and - the output bit error rate as the function of spectrum coverage factor. The simulation rums were repeated for various operating conditions of the receiver. The test was carried out as the next stage of the work on new quality measures of communication in HF radio channels. The results are compatible with those published previously and obtained in laboratory conditions.

articleTitle: Color Television FM Systems — Calculation of Permissible Interference Levels
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Method of calculation of permissible power of radiosignals which interfere with PM communication systems transmitting color television is given. The critierion for calculation is the permissible change of the screen chrominance when taking into account McAdam threshold.

articleTitle: Field Distribution Near the Motor Van at Mobile Radio Reception
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: When radiowaves arrive at metallic body of the motor van local field of disturbance is formed with complex amplitude and polarization structure. The dimentions of disturbance zone for the main component, correspondent to the radiated field by polarization are limited by distance interval 0+ /3 from the body surface of the van. The zone of disturbance increases for cross-polarized components. Correlation between levels of polarized components of the disturbed field depends on the degree of depolarization and the direction of radiowave arrival.

articleTitle: Effective Elimination of Disturbing Ground Reflections by Difraction Screens
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Sector type screens useing for suppression ground reflections is analysed. The optimal variants of the screens are revealed through the analysis of the space characteristics of the created area of suppression and the introduction of the effective coefficient of reflection as the goal function. The experiments done on the real ground surface corroborated their sufficiently high efficiency.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Detection Algorithms of Sequences of Impulse Signals to Changes of Fluctuation Noise Parameters
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An evaluation of the possibility for using optimum and suboptimum radio-receivers synthesized under Neumann-Pearson criterion in conditions when noise parameters are changed in comparison with those under synthésis. Concrete results are given for evaluation of algorithm's sensitivity when detecting impulses' sequence with casual initial phase and amplitude in the presence of narrow-band gaussian noised.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Commutation Interference Taking Stray Modulations into Consideration
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the work of functional assembly for different applications in redio electronic equipment in key mode which results in the appearance of com.mutation interference, the most widely spread type of interference in equipment.

articleTitle: Measurement of Immunity of Domestic Audiofrequency Equipment
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The basic principles of methods of immunity control of domestic-frequency equipment to external electromagnetic fields in the frequency band 20 Hz - 30 MHz are given. The results of experimental investigations of some specimens from series produced equipment (amplifiers, electrical record-players, tape recorders) are presented.

articleTitle: Membrane Effects of Low Intensity Millimeter Wave Irradiation
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It was shown that active sodium ion transport through isolated frog skin as well as the current through polarographic cell with platinimi electrode can be enhanced by the continous MM wave irradiation at low power density (about 1 mW/sm<sup>2</sup>). All effects observed are supposed to be caused by convective mixing of water layers attached to the skin or electrode surfaces. Increase of transport rate through diffusion unstirred layers may be one of the primary mechanisms of biological effects of MM wave irradiation.

articleTitle: Radiation Emitted by Leaders and Intracloud Lightning Discharges Processes and the Fields Resulting at the Ground
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We describe essentially in this communication the specific radiations of leader and intracloud discharges. These measurements, of fields resulting at ground, have been effected in time analysis for 150 Hz - 20 MHz band and in spectrum analysis between 60 - 900 MHz. We present the electromagnetic characteristics of the radiation but also the phenomenal analysis of them for lightning discharges processes, lastly the physical mechanisms of these processes are brought up.

articleTitle: Electronic Equipment and Systems For Radiomonitoring
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper describes receivers suitable for radiomonitoring applications: an LF-HF receiver for 10 kHz to 30 MHz and a VHF-UHF receiver for 20 to 1000 MHz. In both receivers a synthesizer with 10 Hz resolution is used for frequency tuning, the further frequency processing being derived from one crystal oscillator. Setting accuracies of 3 x 10<sup>-7</sup> and 1 x 10<sup>-8</sup> are achieved in the whole operating temperature range. A panoramic adapter suitable for both receivers is described in some detail. Finally the characteristics of microprocessor-controlled frequency-band recording equipment are discussed and examples of recording are presented.

articleTitle: Perturbation of the 50 Hz Noise in the Vicinity of Rivers and Cables
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It results from our considerations and also from experimental data that on the ground surface 50 Hz EMW is propogated perpendicularly to the ground in large regions. So, the magnetic field(MF)has zero vertical component. The theoretical consideration was made on perturbation of HF caused by a long conducting cylinder. It was concluded that in the vicinity of such objects, the vertical component of magnetic field must occur. An evalutation of sensitivity of the method for detection of such a field was made.

articleTitle: A Study on the Improvement of Callus Formation of Fracture by a Specific Change of Electromagnetic Field
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Although various methods have been proposed to improve callus formation by changing the electrical enviroment, the non-invasive inductive coupling method is preferred by the majority of patients as well as physicians. The purpose of this research is to determine the specific change of electromagnetic field which creates the most ideal enviroment for callus formation by comparing eight different pulse train waveforms. Twenty-seven rabbit experiments were completed and results were obtained.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility in the 12 GHZ Band with Regard to Different TV Signal Modulation Methods Used in the TV Broadcasting Terrestrial Network
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of the principal questions which arises when TV broadcasting terrestrial systems in the 12 GHz band are developed is a choice of transmitted signal modulation method. Electromagnetic compatibility of terrestrial and satellite TV broadcasting-systems is one of the factors which determine this choise. The report deals with electromagnetic compatibility of satellite and terrestrial TV broadcasting systems in the 12 GHz band with different TV signal modulation methods in the TV broadcasting terrestrial network. Calculation examples of necessary geographical spacing between satellite and terrestrial TV broadcasting service areas in which co-channel operation using amplitude and frequency modulated TV signals is planned are given. The calculations are based on CCIR documents.

articleTitle: The General Method for Determing Non-Linear Effects by the Curves of Maximum Usable Sensitivity of the Receiver
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The general method for determing non-linear effects of a receiver is described in this report. The method based on measurement of the degree of nonlinerity of the receiver transfer characteristics. In order to determine transfer characteristics the curves of degradation maximum usable sensitivity of the receiver are used. The most important non-linear effects are: degradation maximum usable sensitivity of the receiver, third-order intermodulation, AM cross-modulation and PM cross-modulation. It is shown how we can easily find any non-linear effects of receiver using sensitivity degradation curves.

articleTitle: Immunity Improvement of home Entertainment Electronic Devices
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Amateur radio stations are usually located in close vicinity to home entertainment electronic devices. This explaines our engagement on this field. In the paper are presented simple and inexpensive means to be used for susceptibility limiting, methods applied in measurements and comparative results of measurements with and without protective means. These results show possibility of simple way to immunity improvement when a device is designed. Presented conclusions are valid for any radiocommunication service and other services generating EM fields.

articleTitle: Optimum Methods of Operative Frequency Assignment to Radio Communication Facilities Operating in the Metric Waveband
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The basic principles and algorithms for optimal operative assignment of frequencies to new radio facilities which are just placed in commission are given. They envisage a formation of finite sets of previously assigned and reserve frequencies at which the electromagnetic compatibility between the radio facilities is ensured. A frequency taken from the elements of the sets is assigned to a new radio facility. A selection of a frequency is made according to a prescribed criterion. The basic criteria of selection of frequencies are the following ones: ”the nearest neighbour”, ”the maximum repetition and multiplex of frequency channels” and ”the maximum proximity to the threshold of compatibility”.

articleTitle: EMC Regulations and Methods of Measurement for Sound and Television Broadcast Receivers in the Federal Republic of Germany
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Corresponding to the German legislation the above mentioned receivers, if they are considered for operation in Germany, must fulfill technical regulations. One part of these regulations applies to EMC. That means, that there are laid down limits, which are expected to ensure sufficient immunity against interference of receivers under normal conditions. In the following details with regard to the EMC regulations and to the methods of immunity measurements are described

articleTitle: A Frequency Assignment in Broadcasting Networks Planning Assisted by Computer
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: At the RAI (Radiotelevisione Italiana) a research has been under taken aiming to plan automatically by computer the broadcasting networks (by satellite of terrestrial). The work is not yet finished. The paper describes the main principles on which the adopted method is based, the problems encountered and the points yet under study. Use is made of a digitalized rappresentation of the zone to be planned; RF channels and polarizations are assigned on the basis of the graph theory.

articleTitle: EMC in Wire Telecommunication Networks an Introduction
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Sources of electromagnetic fields affecting telecommunication lines are mentioned. Referring to CCITT documents the state of the art is outlined. Current EMC problems caused by the use of sensitive semiconductor devices in telecommunication installation are specified. Relations of contributions to the EMC Symposium with thoses problems are shown.

articleTitle: The Content of Aminoacids in the Seedlings of PI Sum Sativum L. and Cucumis Sativus L. in the Environment Without Exterior Electromagnetic Field
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It has been found that the content of arginine, proline and glutamic acid increase about 30% in the shoots and roots in the 4— and 6- days old seedlings of Pi sum sativum in the environment without electromagnetic field of 100 kHz to 300 MHz, in comparison to the control conditions. In the 4- and 6-days old seedlings of Cucumis sativus the largest increase was observed in the content of histidine, glutamic acid, glicyne, valine, tyrosine.

articleTitle: On the Selection of Magnetic-Field for Ferrite Loaded Junction in Microwave Devices
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A theoretical investigation carried out on the selection of magnetic for a ferrite loaded junction using in microwave devices is reported. An equation has been developed which relates d.c. biasing magnetic field and the frequency of operation ivolving other design variables such as saturation magnetisation, permeability and gyromagnetic ratio. Selection of magnetic field through this relation reduces the mismatching between the line and the ferrite loaded junction. Design curves are also presented for several ferrites.

articleTitle: Measurement of the 50 Hz Noise Level in Urban and Rural Environments
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Amplitudes of 30 Hz electric and magnetic fields were studied both under laboratory and outdoor conditions. The magnetic field was detested by a coil with ferrite core, and electric one - by a probe condenser or by electrodes inserted into the ground. The milivoltmeter or oscilloscope were used to measure the pre-amplified signal In open area EM-wave perpendicular to the ground was found. Near the electric power lines and appliances no correlation between E and M - field occurred.

articleTitle: Some PLHR Phenomena and Their Explanation
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We consider a theory of power line harmonic radiation (PLHR) interactions, based on a computer simulation of particle trapping by a coherent whistler mode signal. After amplification to a sufficient signal strength (considered to be ∼ 1 pT) the PLH wave distorts the original distribution of energetic electrons. The distribution leads to new gradients in the distribution function and hence new growth rates. Frequency offset, broadening of line bandwidths and upward line drifts are consequences of this wave/particle interaction.

articleTitle: Validation of the Fourth-Power Law in Radio Propagation
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Transmission-loss vs distance relations are confronted with analytic and empirical data. The fourth-power law holds in various terrains, in a three-decade frequency interval, up to the redefined radio horizon. Elementary transmission-loss formulas are accurate in regular open terrains below ca 100 MHz. General formula for irregular terrains is less accurate, but valid in larger frequency and distance ranges.

articleTitle: Collocation Technique for Computing the Undesirable Radiation of a Short Backfire Antenna
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Distribution of the undesirable radiation of an antenna is an important problem concerned with electromagnetic compatibility. A thin-wire model has been used to analyse this problem in the case of a short backfire (SBF) antenna as an example. The wire array is described by the Pocklington's equation which has been solved by applying the piecewise sinusoidal collocation method. The influence of the SBF antenna construction parameters on the side and the back radiation has been modelled. Finally, the results obtained are compared with the experimental data.

articleTitle: A New Cable with Three Conductors as an Active Distributed Parameter Line
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, transmission theory of three conductors line with active coupling between the three conductors is analysed. One of propagation constants of such line could be increasing when an intrinsic co-relation between L,M and C of three conductors is broken put effectively by capacitive or inductive loading. Conditions for stable and mode separable increasing propagation are discussed and three applications of the new transmission line are described. First of them is transmission characteristics of solid state mutual coupling cable loaded by transistors and capacitances periodically, second is gain performance of a triode with long and slender three electrodes and third is posibility of heating plasma by increasing propagation of electromagnetic wave on the three electrodes in plasma.

articleTitle: How Are EMI Tests To Be Managed?
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The following paper addressed various difficulties people. are faced with when meaningful EMI tests are to be performed. The major areas of concern for Hewlett-Packard Company are herein brushed. The information provided was derived from commercial type measurements following CISPR Recommendations, performed worldwide by our different manufacturing divisions.

articleTitle: Computer Program for the Design of Antenna Matching Networks
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This computer program calculates the values of the elements of a three element lumped parameter Pi or Tee antenna matching network. The values are those that will minimize the input reflection coefficient of the antenna plus matching network, over the specified frequency bandwidth, in the mean square sense. The program is written in time-sharing FORTRAN IV and is highly user oriented. The computer will ask a series of questions, most of which are self explanatory, and waits for the user answer. An example illustrates the use of the computer program.

articleTitle: A Global Satellite Study of the 17.8 KHz Naa Transmitter Signal
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The NAA (17.8 kHz) signal from Cutler, Maine (44.5°N, 293°E, Λ = 56.5) was continuously recorded on the satellite Ariel 4 from December 1971 to August 1972. The mean signal at 500 km altitude was determined for day and night conditions and for northern and southern hemispheres as a function of longitude and invariant latitude. Several interesting features were noticed; these give evidence for amplification of the NAA signal by cyclotron resonance with energetic electrons. Comparison is made between the observed wavefield at 500 km and calculations [10]. These authors predict a greater signal strength maximum in the south than the north (by 7 dB) at midnight, whereas the Ariel observations show a greater signal strength maximum in the north both during the day (by 5dB) and during the night (by 9 dB). Reasons for this, and OGO 4 data apparently supporting their prediction, are given. The importance of a strong magnetospherically propagated signal in the conjugate Ionosphere, as a source of interference on the ground with the sub-ionospherically propagated signal is discussed.

articleTitle: Field Measuring and Computing System for Studying Natural VLF Radio Noise with the Method of Diversity Reception
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The field measuring and computing system of diversity reception with the digital filtration by Fourier transformation method was worked out and checked in mobile version. Software of the system allows for real-time processing of experimental data with the subsequent obtaining statistical correlation and spectral characteristics of investigated processes.

articleTitle: Session on EMC and Biology - Introductory Remarks
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problems discussed in the lectures designed for presentation during this Session are of important biological significance. Extremely combined electromagnetic (e-m) fields in the surrounding environment could be a potential hazard to such biological processes as growth, reproduction, immunity and the functions of nervous and endocrine regulatory systems in the living organisms. On the other hand, a highly specified e-m fields are of promising significance for therapeutic application. Therefore it is necessary to develop devices and methods for the assessment of e-m fields in the open space, on surface and inside the human body as well an appropriate applicators of e-m energy for localized hyperthermia.

articleTitle: Impact of Electromagnetic Field and Pulse on the Boiling of Conducting and Nonconducting Fluids
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The studies of electromagnetic pulse and field (EMP and EMF) influence on the boiling of conducting and nonconducting fluids have been conducted theoretically. Present studies are particularly important for EMF and EMP protections of the termal and nuclear power plant heat transport loops, since the boiled fluid is under AC high voltage or magnetic field in normal operations or under EMP impact in abnormal operations triggered by lightnings. In this paper, the boiling model to obtain maximum and minimum heat fluxes in boiling characteristics based on the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability analysis has been modified to consider the effect of EMF and EMP for both conducting and nonconducting fluids.

articleTitle: -NESSY-: Noise Estimation System for Board-Level Circuit Using Electronic Circuit Simulator
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The board—level electronic circuit noise simulator, NESSY (Noise Estimation SYstem), is a quantitative analysis program for optimization of circuit pattern design implemented in APL. It features segmentation of circuit pattern, calculation of the partial capacitance and inductance, simulation of partial equivalent element circuit by ICD and optimization of pattern arrangement.

articleTitle: Measurements of Electric and Magnetic Fields of Very Low Frequencies in Unurbanized Environment
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Magnetic and electrict fields of the frequencies from 1 Hz to 1 kHz occurring in an unurbanized environment were studied. Electric field was detected by metal rod probes inserted in the ground and magnetic fields were detected by a multiturn coil. For the frequencies above 50Hz the harmonics of the mains were found to dominate and for the frequencies below 50Hz a frequency of about 8Hz was distinguished.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Applicability of Mathematical Models in E M C
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Some specific EMC computer codes are described. Their use is presented. The application of a computer code to the study of interface circuits is described. The results are evaluated with the aim of finding improved performances of the interface circuits.

articleTitle: On the Suppression of Magnetic Induced Interfering Voltages in Four-Wire and Three-Wire Transmission Circuits
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Inductively coupled in interfering voltages can be compensated to a large extend by using three-wire or four-wire lines with two induction loops, whereby the receiver forms the difference between the two induced interfering voltages. A general model and three elementary transmission circuits of such kind are described in this paper. Practical results confirm the theoretical considerations. Concluding remarks refer to generalization as well as to known line configurations.

articleTitle: Measures Against Noise Interference in Analogue Telephone Lines
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the problem of noise interference of telephone lines by electric railways, in particular when thyristor controlled traction is used. At present, the calculation of induced noise voltages is only possible with an insufficient accuracy, but efforts are going on in CCITT to improve the calculating methods. In UIC a special Committee ORE A.122, studying thyristor applications in railway systems, has carried out 1976 - 1978 comprehensive investigations in France and Poland. In conclusion of these studies measures are proposed to reduce the noise voltages. These measures concern the railway traction with AC and DC as well as the telecommunication installations. Finally a scheme of planning guidelines is given in a table based on the experience of UIC/ORE.

articleTitle: Height Characteristics of UHF Television Waves
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The present paper describes results from measurements of height-patterns for UHF television waves at 10∼150 m high in their propagation paths such as the water surface, rural, city suburb and mountains, which is necessary for prediction and analysis of ranges of interference to TV waves by high structures such as buildings and power transmission lines.

articleTitle: Active Distributed Parameter Lines with Ground Return
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Starting with Maxwell's equations, it is shown that wave propagation along a wire above a dissipative ground exposed to an external electromagnetic field can be reduced to an active dispersive distributed parameter line with active source elements and passive circuit parameters. The generalized transmission line equations with a series electromotive force and shunt current source are derived directly from the boundary conditions and the equation of continuity at the wire surface and are examined physically by applying integral forms of Maxwell's equations. The active voltage and current distribution along the line is known from an external electromagnetic field, while the passive circuit parameters consist of the generalized series impedance and the parallel admittance. All the problems of coupling, induction and interference to a transmission line with ground return can be treated on the basis of these equations by giving source terms appropriate to an environment. A couple of examples are given.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of the Interference Susceptibility of Automatic Bridge Measuring Compensator with Pulse Bridge Feeding
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Mathematical model of the influence of the additive interference of random type on the accuracy of the digital automatic bridge measuring compensator with pulse feeding and digit-by-digit balancing is given. Interference is described by a harmonic series with deterministic or random /in reference to the geginning of the bridge balancing/ phase spectrum. This model is realized as a computer programm. Main inner cycle of the program is repeated for each phase of modelling digit-by-digit bridge balancing in the presence of interference. External cycle of the program provides for statistic modelling. Program allows for finding statistical characteristics of the errors of digital output readings of the compensator due to interference. Model may be used for EMC calculations for the use of the compensator with other instruments containing interference sources.

articleTitle: EMI of Lightning with Digital Communication Systems
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: EM-radiation from cloud located lightning discharges made high EMI with PCM-communication systems. This is due to a relatively low maximum permissible noise level in a conventional PCM-system (about 30 mV), to a high level of radiated field pulses (in the range of 20 V/m at a distance of 5 km) in the particular time scale, and to the predominantly horisontal direction of cloud flashes. In addition to this, the number of cloud flashes is much higher as the number of ground flashes.

articleTitle: MIL-STD-461 Interference Data as a Measure of the Spectral Density of a Signal
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For data to be useful it must be able to be measured accurately and consistently and provide some predictive power. This paper addresses the way interference measurements are made by the primary American Military Electromagnetic Compatibility Specification. The properties of accuracy, consistency and predictiveness are found lacking. Some improvements are suggested.

articleTitle: A Circuit Model of Lightning Discharge to a Transmission Line
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Authors represent some results of the near field change signal due to the progressing leader which include straight downward and refracting somewhere along the way backward or forward the observing site. They are obtained by calculation and represented as the graphic method which have the normalized scales of nΔx/H on the axis of abscissa and of ∑ ΔEn4πε<inf>0</inf>D/2ρ on the vertical axis. On the other hand some oscillographic records have been obtained in the field which are of much value to compare with the results obtained by calculation.

articleTitle: Examination of Electromagnetic Interference in the Range of 0-50 kHz
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper the measuring set for automatic recording of electromagnetic interference level is presented and the results of measurements and the procedures of their analysis are discussed. The measurements were carried out in Warsaw suburban environs. The measuring set consists of HP 3580A spectrum analyser and automatic recording circuit with A/D converter. The results are recorded by DT 105S printer. The preprocessing program changes the number of A/D converter levels into corresponding values of magnetic field strength expressed in dB/µA/m or in dB/pT. The statistical analysis program enables mean value, standard deviation, median, quantiles of 99.5% and 0.5% to be computed as well as minimum and maximal values to be chosen The results are presented as frequency-varying in the range of 0-50 kHz for various time intervals of day and night and as time of day-varying for various frequencies of the range examined. The differences between working days and holidays and between different times of day (morning-noon-avening-night) as well as minimum and maximal values of all results evaluated. The results are compared with those published by CCIR and with those obtained in Washington (USA).

articleTitle: Differences of Biological Effects of Simple and Combined Electromagnetic Fieldsxx
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Short-term exposure of rate to microwaves at SAH 10-15 W/kg and repeated exposure to simple or combined e-m fields at SAR 2.5-3 W/kg or low incident intensity changed such parameters as body mass gain, mass, water content and conductivity of salivary gland, and Na<sup>+</sup> K<sup>+</sup>, Ca<sup>++</sup> concentrations in this gland and in the brain· The combined e-m fields were more effective in this respect.

articleTitle: Antenna Isolation by the Longitudinal Screen
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The presented experimental results prove the existance of the effect of local suppression of the electromagnetic field by flat conducting structures (plates) orientated in the polarization plane of the electric field along the direction of the wave propagation. A physical reason of the protected effect is pointed out to be interference of the wave passed near the conducting plate surface with the component of the electromagnetic field due to the edge wave channelled along the plate edge. It is pointed out that the possibility of suppression by longitudinal elements may be effectively used for isolation of antennas placed in free space and near the objects of different configuration and electrical properties.

articleTitle: Direct Satellite Broadcasting - A Network Analysis
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a simulation model of the satellite broadcasting system to be used for investigating internal compatibility. Allowance had been made for interference from all transmitters operating in the system according to the WARC-12 GHz plan of 1977, the specific noise of the receivers as well as the conditions of radio wave propagation. In the model no interference caused by other radio communication services or any other sources that are not components of the system under consideration had been taken into account. The exemplary results of calculations of the signal-to-noise ratio to be recorded in Poland from the POL 132B and D 087B transmitters are given.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility and the International Union of Radio Science
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: URSI being the international scientific Union for telecommunications has several Commissions interested in the subjects treated in Symposia on Electromagnetic Compatibility. A survey is given of URSI Commissions and their interests. The subjects of Lightning and of permanent damage to electrical equipment, caused by electrostatic discharges are covered in more detail.

articleTitle: Television Receiver Local Oscillator Harmonic Radiation: Statistical Data
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radiation from local oscillators of tuners of TV receivers is discussed. More than 1300 individual measuring results on 18 tuners led to the conclusion that the levels of radiation on oscillator frequencies may be evaluated from the following formula: I<inf>n</inf> = I<inf>1</inf> - a./lg n/ in which: I<inf>n</inf> - mean value of the n—th oscillator harmonic /voltage or the field strength/, I<inf>1</inf> - the same for the base oscillator frequency.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Receiving Circular Loop Antenna in Dissipative Media
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Analysis of a receiving circular loop antenna immersed in a dissipative medium, placed near different sources and boundary with other media has been presented in the paper. The integral equation for current distribution in the antenna was presented and then solved by applying the method of Fourier-series-expansion. From the solution follows that the current in the antenna depends mainly on EM field components (electric and magnetic) at the antenna center. This conclusion is true when the antenna is electrically small [1,5]. But when the antenna is placed in the near-zone this limitations is not sufficient. Additionally the antenna diameter have to be small compared with the distance to the nearest EM field source.

articleTitle: Analysis of Nonlinear Phenomena Occuring in the Presence of Narrow Band Additifs Interferences
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is necessary to introduce some parameters charakterizing receivers in the complex way and some methods of analysis of circuits and devices for optimization. The Volterra-Wiener series for solving these problems are the most adequate method. This method sures good convergence for the signal which amplitude is result anassumed dynamics of the receiver.

articleTitle: Amplitude, Time and Frequency Digital Signal Processing for Noise Analysis in High Voltage Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The essential effects of noise in communication systems are well known. It interferes directly on the error rate in digital data transmission or telemetering, and it causes undesirable effects on the security and reliability of teleprotection channels. Due to the above and referring to noise in Power Line Carrier (PLC) communication channels, this paper presents the statistical techniques required to perform an evaluation of carrier frequency noise characteristics. Noise analysis has been executed in amplitude, time and frequency domains and its results are shown.

articleTitle: Comparison of Three Computation Methods for Sommerfeld Integrals
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, we compare three numerical methods for Sommerfeld integrals calculation. These integrals are encountered in the radiated field components in presence of half medium with finite conductivity. It is essential to accurately evaluate Sommerfeld integrals; analytical and approximate evaluation are in fact not available for all ranges of operating conditions, particulary in the proximal region of the electromagnetic sources. The integrals are computed by three methods : - déformations of the integration path (Lytle et Lager)[l] - integration along the real axis (Faure)[2] - method of the steepest descent path (Rahmat-Samii Parhami et Mittra) [3]

articleTitle: Modelling of Lightning
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Modern telecommunication is more and nore using pulse technology. At present the necessary information for a model of the lightning pulse environment (i e the distribution of amplitudes, durations and separations of the pulses) is not available. The pulse structure of the leader and of the return stroke stages are available in required detail. However, the structure of the cloud events are scarcely known. Therefore it is important that more attention is paid to the pulse structure of the cloud flash in future research.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Television Video Recorders to Radio Frequency Fields
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Television Video Recorders are quickly becoming popular. Millions are in use in densely populated areas. The sensitivity to harmonics of near-by transmitters will be reduced with low-pass filtering at the transmitter output. Any overload effects at the vhf-uhf-tuners must be reduced by inserting isolating transformers at the antenna input. In some countries specifications exist for this sort of immunity. Unfortunately, the severe problem is direct field penetration into the video section which is sensitive to all frequencies from 1 MHz to almost 10 MHz.

Author Keywords: Susceptibility of Video Recorders in Radio Frequency Fields.
TEM Cell for generating defined E-Fields

articleTitle: Analysis of Modal Parameters of the Wire-Ground System in a Wide Frequency Range
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An accurate solution for propagation constant of wire-ground system was first obtained by Grinberg and Bonshtedt, Kikuchi, Lavrov and later by Wait and Wedepohl. However, there has been no complete numerical solution for the entire frequency range, with a correct physical interpretation of the results. This paper analyses analytically and numerically an accurate solution for a 10<inf>2</inf>-10<inf>9</inf> Hz frequency range, with wire impedance taken into consideration. It is shown that there exist two main modes in the entire frequency range. The solution corresponding to the larger value of the attenuation constant approaches the Carson solution for the wire-ground system at low frequencies and to the Zenneck solution for the plane surface wave near the ground at high frequencies. The solution for the smaller value of the attenuation constant approaches the Zenneck solution at low frequencies and the Sommerfeld solution for the solitary wire at high frequencies. The relationships between the wire current and the ground current which permit calculation of wave propagation characteristics for a given line excitation, are obtained.

articleTitle: Determining the Receiving and Interfering Zone in Mobile Radiocommunications by the AID of Computer
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: While planning the mobile radio stations, the greatest difficulty is high-quality and quick determination of receiving zone and interfering signal zone of base radio station. The use of computer for graphical representation and determination of usable signal zones, unwanted signal zones and interfering zones are described in this paper. In older to determine these zones, a computer readable relief model as well as die CCIR curves together with correction for clearance angle are used. To determine one zone, the computer has calculated the field level in more than 7.000 points. The results of computer calculations are checked in 123 measuring points lenghth of which beeing 1 km on the road long about 700 km.

articleTitle: Dynamic Compatibility in Systems with State Identification Subsystem
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The performance of communication systems can be improved by adapting their operation to the state of the whole system. The methods of acquisation and utilization of the information about the state of the system are described and fundamental relationships between the quality of performance of the communication systems and the size of the state identification subsystem are derived.

articleTitle: An RC Circuit Model of Lightning Beams on a Very Tall Structure
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An RC circuit model has been developed to predict the effect of tall structure on the lightning characteristics. The results show that the total charge in a downward lightning flash and the percentage of the upward leader from tall structures are predicted to be increases with increasing structure heights, and this prediction agrees well with the recent lightning observations.

articleTitle: Dynamic Behaviour of Voltage Limiting Components
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the dynamic properties of semiconductor diodes and metal-oxide varistors proceeding from the basic conditions of application of voltage limiting components. In this connection especially the behaviour of these components for a stress with surge voltages of a short rise time will be discussed. Furthermore the influence of d.c. bias voltages as well as the effects of series connections of several semiconductor diodes on the time behaviour have been examined.

articleTitle: RFI Prevention in Industrial Networks Supplying Static Power Converters
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radio frequency interference (RFI) generated by periodic thyristor switching is an important factor in the design and arrangement of low voltage supply networks and digital and analog data transmission in industrial plants with equipment containing static power converters (SPC). This paper deals with RFI generated by converters in the frequency range 10 kHz to 30 MHz, its propagation and coupling with signal lines. Some recommendation concerning SPC connection to the mains and cabling arrangement are given.

articleTitle: Waveguide Applicators for Biomedical Application: An Accurate Analysis of Power Coupling in Inhomogeneous Biomedical Media.
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The e.m. characteristics of apertures fed by standard waveguides ended by an iris of general shape are considered; the aperture admittances along with the radiation pattern in the biological medium are evaluated as a function of frequency, iris shape, and of tissue parameters. In this near-field situation the sources are strongly coupled to the human tissues and therefore the radiation characteristics of the aperture are obtained by solution of coupled integro-differential equations that is performed numerically by means of the method of moments.

articleTitle: Antennas Penetrating the Ground Interface Illuminated by a Non-Uniform Electromagnetic Field
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We present a study of a vertical electric antenna penetrating the interface which separates a free space and a lossy half space. The antenna can be excited by an inhomogenous incident plane wave. The model used is the antenna integral equation, which includes the SOMMERFELD integrals, to take the interface effect into account. Our approach employs a Galerkin's moment method with linear piecewise functions as expansion and testing functions. The numerical results show the current distribution on the surface of the antenna, and the input impedance.

articleTitle: Transient Induced Voltages in Communication and Control Systems in Large Industrial Building which is Stroken by Lighting
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Lightning, striking a building can cause damages or interferences in normal operations of communication, controling and measuring systems inside the structure. This paper is primary concerned with the model measurements of lightning current distribution in building constructed with metal or reinforcing steel. Thanks to these measurements it was possible to calculate voltages induced in electrical Systems installed in industrial building which is stroken by lightning.

articleTitle: Viscosity of Bicmolecules in Microwave Field
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The viscometric data from protein solutions irradiated by microwaves are presented here. Specific absorption rate /SAR/ of microwaves was not greater then 1 mW/kg when the dependence of viscosity on frequency was measured, and in the range of 1-70 mW/kg in the case of single /3.5 GHz/ frequency. No significant changes in the viscosity coefficient of protein solutions were observed neither as the function of frequency nor power intensity of microwaves.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Effects of A - C Transmission Lines on Extensive Underground Conductor Earthed Through Impedances
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents the method of calculation of currents and potentials excited by electromagnetic effects of a transmission power line on infinitely long underground conductor earthed through impedance. The analysis treats to arbitrary buried conductor using an electrical transmission line theory. The calculation take into account the additional conductive effect of the current flowing through the earthing impedance on the potential distribution along the conductor. The method presented is illustrated by examples.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness of Reinforced Concrete Against Electromagnetic Waves
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: No satisfactory theory for the calculation of the shielding against electromagnetic radiation of reinforced concrete has as yet been found. A solution to this problem, presented in this paper, is based on the idea, that the power of the inpinging electromagnetic radiation is distributed between the reinforcing steel and the concrete in the ratio of their wave admittances. The shielding effectiveness is therefore determined by the specific electrical, dielectrical and magnetic properties of both mediums, their flux cross sections and wave frequency. For this treatment, Poynting, Maxwell and d'Alembert relations are used. To illustrate the presented method the shielding effectiveness of reinforced concrete against NEMP and lightning radiation is calculated.

articleTitle: Intermodulation Distortion Minimizing in H.F. Amplifier of a Marine Radiocommunication Receiver
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The H.F. amplifier of communication receiver should assure minimization of intermodulation distortions. On the base of measurements and analysis as assumption of restriction to small nonlinearites with good approximation of Volterra-Wiener series was made. In order to minimization the intermodulation distortions one should make a proper choise of circuit configuration, active devices and working points.

articleTitle: Attenuation of Medium-Frequency Radiowaves on Mountainious Pathes
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For the prognosis of the attenuation function W of ground radiowaves in highlands, there was investigated the propagation of MW radiowaves on pathes with various electrical properties, relief and vegetation. For the purpose of calculating the electromagnetic fields we followed the method of numerical solution of the one-dimensional integral equation for the attenuation function W on electrically inhomogeneous multisectional pathes. To define the module of the attenuation function there were conducted measurements of field strength of the radiobroadcasting station 560 kHz on two typical Transbaicalian pathes about 200 km length. The attenuation on a wooded-mountainious path is 3-8 higer than on a hilly path without forest. Taking into account local meaning of the surface impedance, "homogeneous" sections were destinguished. The impedances of wooded sections were defined into model of horisontally layered structure, the upper layer of which being formed of wooded cover with б= 1,9.10<sup>-5</sup> S/m and ε= 1,3. The obtained results allow for more precise prognosis of the attenuation of LW-MW radiowaves in highlands.

articleTitle: The Resistibility of Components of Electronic Telecommunication Devices Against Overvoltages and Overcurrents
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of the most economical ways for solving the protection of electronic devices against overvoltages from telecommunication lines is to achieve their sufficient resistibility by means of selecting proper components in input circuits. In the paper, the basic methods of testing the resistibility of components in accordance with the values and the duration of overvoltages to be expected at the line end are suggested and some results of the testing of resistors, capacitors and semiconductor components are given.

articleTitle: Natural Electromagnetic Earth Field at ELF
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The report contains the research results of horizontal interorthogonal components of natural electric E<inf>h</inf> and magnetic H<inf>h</inf> fields at the ”air-ground” boundary in the central part of Asia far from the world thunderstorm centers (spectral characteristics at I4 - I20 Hz range, their space and time variations, the eigenfrequencies and Q - values of the earth-ionosphere cavity). The radionoise spectral density diurnal variation accords with the world-wide thunderstorm activity. The prevalent direction of the radionoise arrival is established. The experimental results are of practical interest for the noise environment prediction and electromagnetic sounding of the earth crust.

articleTitle: Criteria of Failure Detection in Protection Circuit Structures Used in Transmission Facilities
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to secure EMC of transmission facilities, especially to protect them against pulse interference, a number of principles proved useful which are mainly used in multiplex systems. Protection circuit structures must meet two requirements. They should 1. adhere to communiation parameters in case of operation 2. ensure protection against danger/interference in case of harmful effects To know their functional reliability or to detect in time when protection is impaired are important quality criteria. Different protection circuit structures and structural elements are classified and compared as to their failure susceptibility permitting to derive fundamental failure statements.

articleTitle: Shielding and Grounding Concept for Non-Stationary Communication Facilities
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Non-stationary switching and transmission facilities being mainly container-mounted must be protected against electromagnetic danger or interference, especially in case of mobile use. In dependence on instrumentation the container must ensure a minimum damping effect. In this paper a complex shielding concept is presented taking into consideration, from the viewpoint of shielding technique, top requirements of shielding material, doors, windows, cable entries, grounding etc.

articleTitle: Some Questions of Investigation the Natural Electromagnetic Field of the Earth in the Frequency Range of 10-200 HZ at Middle Latitudes of the USSR
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper the results of the experimental investigations of horisontal magnetic and horisontal electric components of the natural electromagnetic field are presented in the frequency range of 10-200 Hz at middle latitudes of the USSR. The statistical and spectral characteristics of field, the data on the Shumann resonance frequencies and the fine structure of spectra are presented.

articleTitle: Effect of Propagation Conditions of the Tropospheric Wave on the VHF and UHF Coverage in the South Baltic Area
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The coverage of VHF and UHF stations depends on propagation conditions of the tropospheric wave. Basing on many years' statistical data, investigations of the long-term radiorefractivity distribution in the south Baltic area were carried out. The influence of the annual cycle was examined. Further, an attempt has been undertaken to prove the influence of the air mass on propagation conditions of the tropospheric wave. The results of the study make possible to obtain available data necessary to improve the quality of estimation of the coverage of VHF and UHF stations.

articleTitle: Abnormal Increasing of Radio Noise in Breaking Ag Contact and Its Suppression Methods
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radio–interference wave caused by the arc and the surge in breaking contacts has been known to disturb various electronic equipments. At Ag contacts, a radio interference field of relatively high level occurs in circuit current 2 ∼ 3 A. Its cause was found to be the surge voltage owing to the quasi-arc-chopping. It is furthermore discussed undesired or useful suppression methods for radio-interference in the frequency region 0.1 ∼ 10 MHz

articleTitle: Generation of Electromagnetic Fields for Receiver Immunity Measurements: Some Relevant Problems
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The TEM cell method is widely used to generate strong fields in immunity measurements; unfortunately, the cell dimensions required to test TV receivers are so large as to limit the maximum useable frequency to a value between 100 and 200 MHz. Therefore, in the frequency range from 100 MHz to 1 GHz, the methods proposed by IEC and CISPR are based on a radiating dipole in free space or in an anechoic room, the height of the dipole being fixed at 3/4 λ or variable from 1 to 4 m in order to have the maximum interference on the receiver under test. The main problems concerning these methods are the uniformity of the generated field in the volume occupied by the receiver under test and, when an open-air site is used, the distant radiation which can interfere with other radio services. These problems are discussed for the IEC and CISPR methods and the improvements in using a corner-reflector antenna are considered in order to have an indoor method without the need of an expensive anechoic room.

articleTitle: The Intensity of Electromagnetic Noise in the Plasmasphere of the Earth
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The typical variations of ELF and VLF noise intensity are presented for various conditions in the Earth's plasmasphere. The daily variation /in LT/ of noise at f < 1 kHz has a powerful maximum at noon /Fig. 1a/, This may be seen both under quiet and under disturbed conditions. At f > 1 kHz /see Fig. 1b for f = 1.6 kHz/ the noon maximum is only manifested when Kp > 2 and L> 1.5. Otherwise the maximum of noise intensity occurs at night and the noise level is low. Such an inversion of the daily variation at VLF frequencies when geomagnetic disturbances increase is likely to be connected with changing energetic particle spectra in the inner radiation belt [12, 14]. Fig. 1c shows the L-dependence of the noise intensity at f = 1.6 and 2.5 kHz. One may see the overall increase of intensity with rising Kp-index and the decrease of the L value where the intensity has its maximum. Obviously the latter reflects the movement of the plasmapause. We conclude that the maximum in the L-dependence is just determined by plasmaspheric hiss [8, 12,15). The case study of the connection between energetic electron fluxes and the ELF noise intensity at 0.5 kHz leads us to the conclusion that the highest noise level is observed in the slot between the outer and the inner rediation belt [8]. The L-coordinate of the slot and of the noise level maximum are moving together in the course of the geomagnetic storm development / Fig. 2/. This figure shows also a second low-level maximum of noise at L< 2. That maximum is due to the source of ionospheric noise    which was established in the topside ionosphere [14]. Using the ELF and VLF measurements made by various satellites /INJUN-3 and -5, 0G0-1, -3 and -6, ARIEL-3, INTERCOSMOS-3 and -5/ we have constructed a generalized altitude dependence of the noise intensity over the equator /Fig. 3/. Despite the fact that in this study we use the data obtained in different periods of time and with different measuring devices, the fluctuation of the mean values is not very large /not more than 16 dB according to Fig. 3/.

articleTitle: Digital Terrain MAP for Television and Land Mobile Radio
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The conversion of terrain data into digital form allows to employ the computer in order to perform the most tedious work in analysis of VHF/UHF radio systems - profile extraction and analysis. In the above mentioned application the essential matter is exactness of terrain representation. In the paper, the accuracy of automatically extracted terrain elevation profiles is analyzed for various interpolation formulas, and for various terrain irregularity. The results confirm that the map may be used in analysis and design of vhf/uhf broadcasting and land mobile systems.

articleTitle: Computer Aid in Design of Low-Power TV Network for Efficient Use of Spectrum Space
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper, the procedure of computer aided design of low-power tv network is described. The process of designing is divided into several stages. In the following stages the transmitting station characteristics such as location, radiated power, antenna height and pattern are determined for each transmitter, in consideration of the terrain configuration, environment, and population density distribution. Then, in the final stage the channel assignment is performed. At each stage, the computerized techniques are imployed which allow to optimize the spectrum space use.

articleTitle: Dielectric Loaded Open Waveguide Scanning Antenna
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The radiation characteristics of a ferrite loaded open waveguide radiator are studied. The antena, is shown to be capable of steering the beam over a±45° sector off axis without significant pattern degradation. Angle of the steering is found to depend on d.c. biasing magnetic field. And the sense of deviation in the beam off axis is found to depend on the direction of d.c. biasing magnetic field. Substantial agreement is observed between theoretical and expenmental results.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility and the New Zealand Radio Amateur
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Interference to broadcasting receivers, television receivers, sound reproducing apparatus, and other electronic apparatus has been caused by radio amateurs in New Zealand. They have also experienced interference from television receivers, digital and computing equipment.

articleTitle: Threshold Signal Detection for EMC in Non-Uniform, Non-Gaussian EMI Fields
publicationTitle: Seventh International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The main features of the derivations of optimum threshold detection algorithms in non-gaussian noise fields are sketched, when the receiving antenna (or array) consists of M discrete elements (or arrays) such that the overall dimensions of the array are large enough compared to the wavelengths of the desired input (narrow-band) signal that the EMI field is non-uniform (i.e., not completely correlated) over the array. This allows for possible improvements in processing gain by taking advantage of spatial, as well as temporal, sampling of the fields received by the array. Various results for optimum coherent and incoherent threshold detection are indicated, including the effects of fading and doppler "smear" and the rôle of the proper bias term in the algorithms. In addition to specific classes of algorithms, performances in terms of error probabilities is determined for both optimum and suboptimum detectors, and the rôle of spatial sampling, with adaptive, weighted beam forming is described. Sufficient conditions for asymptotic as well as local optimality are noted. The results are in canonical form, i.e., independent of the particular physical quantities involved. Two main classes of EMI are distinguished, as before: Class A and B interference [l]-[3], [6], now developed as space-time fields. The approach here is parametric-adaptive, based on the underlying statistical physics.
